core_thesis: Solving ill-posed seismic inverse problems with neural operators requires disentangling physical observability, neural learnability, and cross-structure transferability: while multimodal sensing and symmetry-aware pairwise supervision successfully resolve bilateral damage ambiguity on a single structure, cross-structure parameter dispersion exposes a fundamental direction–magnitude decoupling where directional sensitivity transfers zero-shot across topologies while finite damage separation collapses to the symmetric mean.

verified_contributions.title: Bilateral Non-Identifiable Near-Null Space Under Symmetric Horizontal Sensing
verified_contributions.evidence: OpenSees transient dynamic simulations in Phase 1 and Jacobian SVD in Phase 5 established that State A and State B produce horizontal floor acceleration differences <0.14% (I_AB = 5.6), confirming that bilateral ambiguity is a physical near-null space property.

verified_contributions.title: Noise-Whitened Fisher Information Framework for Asymmetric Multimodal Observability
verified_contributions.evidence: Phase 5.5 noise-whitened directional Fisher sensitivity analysis proved that vertical acceleration (S1, sqrt(I_AB)=1829.6) and multimodal sensing (S4, sqrt(I_AB)=2270.5) amplify bilateral sensitivity by >300x over horizontal sensing (S0, sqrt(I_AB)=5.6), moving v_AB out of the numerical near-null space.

verified_contributions.title: Symmetry-Aware Graph Neural Operator with Matched Bilateral Pair Supervision
verified_contributions.evidence: Phase 6.2 benchmark on single-structure SOURCE_A (N=30 held-out evaluations across 15 disjoint pairs) demonstrated that explicit directional and margin supervision elevates bilateral attribution from 50.0% to 80.0% under S1 (p=0.0014) and 90.0% under S4 (p=9.0e-6, cos=+0.9420, sep=0.1671).

verified_contributions.title: Empirical Proof that Physical Observability is Necessary but Insufficient for Learnability
verified_contributions.evidence: Phase 6.2 configuration S2 (column axial strain) exhibited strong directional Fisher sensitivity (sqrt(I_AB)=1344.2) yet collapsed to 50.0% attribution (cos=+0.1047, sep=0.0003), demonstrating an observability vs learnability gap caused by gradient dominance of high-amplitude floor accelerations.

conditional_contributions.title: Zero-Shot Transferability of Directional Damage Sensitivity Across Topological Boundaries
conditional_contributions.evidence: In Phase 7 and the budget ablation, continuous directional sensitivity transferred to unseen frame parameters (L2A cos=+0.841, L2B cos=+0.813) and an unseen 4-story frame (L3 cos=+0.798, with individual seeds reaching +0.955), but finite-state discrete attribution did not transfer (remaining at 50.0%).
conditional_contributions.caveat: Transfer is verified strictly for the continuous directional orientation vector, not for discrete damage state classification.

conditional_contributions.title: Empirical Delineation of Training Budget in Multi-Structure Finite-Separation Collapse
conditional_contributions.evidence: Scaling optimization budget by 8.3x (12 to 100 epochs) across 72 evaluations refined directional alignment (+0.467 to +0.850) but produced zero change in discrete attribution (flat at 50.0%), ruling out undertraining as the explanation.
conditional_contributions.caveat: Demonstrates that optimization budget within standard AdamW cannot resolve multi-structure separation collapse; does not mathematically prove impossibility under alternate architectures or loss formulations.

phase_chain.question: Does symmetric horizontal floor acceleration sensing induce physical non-identifiability between bilateral damage states?
phase_chain.method: OpenSeesPy dynamic simulations of 3-story frame comparing State A (left column 30%) vs State B (right column 30%).
phase_chain.main_result: Horizontal floor accelerations differ by <0.14%, establishing empirical non-identifiability.

phase_chain.question: Can a 1D Fourier Neural Operator approximate the forward transient dynamic mapping accurately?
phase_chain.method: 1D Spectral Conv forward operator trained on earthquake-induced structural acceleration traces.
phase_chain.main_result: Forward FNO achieves NRMSE < 0.05 (~0.038), validating operator approximation capability.

phase_chain.question: Can standard Inverse FNO invert sparse acceleration signals without mean-seeking collapse?
phase_chain.method: Direct inverse mapping trained with MSE loss vs physics-informed regularization (Sparsity L1 + TV + Cycle Consistency).
phase_chain.main_result: Naive MSE collapses to diffuse zero-mean state; regularization enforces sparsity but cannot resolve bilateral ambiguity.

phase_chain.question: How does spatial sensor placement and sparsity govern localization and severity accuracy?
phase_chain.method: Systematic story-level sensor placement sweep (1-sensor, 2-sensor, full 3-story).
phase_chain.main_result: Graceful degradation with sparsity, but horizontal floor sensors cannot differentiate symmetric columns regardless of sensor density.

phase_chain.question: What is the mathematical structure of the parameter-to-response sensitivity mapping?
phase_chain.method: Finite-difference Jacobian linearization, SVD singular spectra, and Fisher Information Matrix across S0..S4.
phase_chain.main_result: S0 possesses near-zero singular values aligned with v_AB, proving that bilateral ambiguity is a physical near-null space property (I_AB = 5.6).

phase_chain.question: Which sensor modalities physically resolve bilateral ambiguity under noise-whitened conditions?
phase_chain.method: Noise-whitened Jacobian J_w = Sigma^(-1/2) J and directional Fisher sensitivity I_AB = v_AB^T F_w v_AB.
phase_chain.main_result: sqrt(I_AB): S4 (2270.5) > S1 (1829.6) > S2 (1344.2) >> S0 (5.6). Adding vertical acceleration amplifies sensitivity by >300x.

phase_chain.question: Can a symmetry-aware dual-stream Graph FNO resolve bilateral damage states under unpaired supervision?
phase_chain.method: DualStreamGFNO decomposing representations into symmetric H+ and antisymmetric H- latent subspaces with hierarchical heads.
phase_chain.main_result: Improves overall localization, but bilateral attribution remains at 50% chance level under unpaired supervision.

phase_chain.question: Why did ordinary supervised learning fail to separate bilateral states on observable configurations (S1, S4)?
phase_chain.method: Sensor utilization tracing, gradient norm tracking, and input attribution analysis.
phase_chain.main_result: Gradient dominance: high-power horizontal floor accelerations drive 98%+ of early loss reduction, ignoring subtle vertical/strain signals.

phase_chain.question: Does explicit bilateral pair supervision force the network to utilize asymmetric sensing and separate states?
phase_chain.method: Matched bilateral pair training with directional loss L_dir and contrastive margin loss L_pair.
phase_chain.main_result: Single-structure SOURCE_A (N=30 evaluations): S4 achieves 90.0% (p=9.0e-6, cos=+0.9420, sep=0.1671); S1 achieves 80.0% (p=0.0014); S0 remains 50.0%; S2 reveals learnability gap (50.0%).

phase_chain.question: Does the bilateral inverse mapping generalize across varied structural configurations and unseen topologies?
phase_chain.method: 530 OpenSees simulations across 120 PEER earthquakes, 10 structural configurations, protocols P1 and P2, tested across L1, L2A, L2B, L3.
phase_chain.main_result: Under pristine physics conditioning (E_norm=1.0), discrete attribution drops to 50.0% across all levels, while directional cosine remains consistently positive (+0.43 to +0.48).

phase_chain.question: Is the clean Phase 7 attribution collapse caused primarily by undertraining (12 epochs)?
phase_chain.method: Controlled budget scaling [12, 25, 50, 100 epochs] across 3 seeds (42, 101, 2024), P1/P2, and S0/S1/S4 (72 evaluations) on Mac GPU.
phase_chain.main_result: Budget scaling increases directional cosine (+0.467 -> +0.852 -> +0.897 -> +0.850, individual seeds up to +0.996), but discrete attribution remains pinned at 50.0% (sep ~ 1.8e-5 << 0.30).

phase6_2_bilateral_result.statistical_test: Two-sided exact binomial test vs chance (p0=0.5)
